_doc: B1 (ops audit): move the cross-machine watch of iMac ops · 01 from box to MBA<->iMac. register.sh prints the orca commands (dry-run). The create is --disabled. <MBA 新任务 id> is filled from register.sh --mba-id after the MBA task exists. 'before' = live config read 2026-10-21 19:1x SGT (orca automations show, read-only).

create.name: ops · 29 心跳互查 MBA（盯 iMac ops · 01）
create.why: replaces box 94e4b0bc (same rrule and grace); MBA's Orca has no environment for the iMac, so heartbeat-watch reads the iMac's run records through scripts/orca-via-ssh, installed next to heartbeat-watch.sh in ~/.orca-state/bin (README step 1); empty environment = the Orca that HB_ORCA reaches. Precheck timeout 330 (box: 240): worst case 296 s = 3 tries x the wrapper's 70 s ssh cap + 2 x 8 s + one list call (70 s) when no heartbeat has been seen yet and none is fresh; plus about 4 s to start. 330 s is longer than the 5 min schedule and heartbeat-watch.sh does not lock its state file, so the precheck runs under /usr/bin/lockf -k -t 0 with this task's own lock file in ~/.orca-state/heartbeat-watch (README step 1 creates the directory on the MBA): a round that starts while the previous one is still running exits 75 without starting heartbeat-watch (no state read or write, no @@HB); Orca records any non-zero precheck exit as skipped. A lock that stays held would skip every round, so lockf runs under ~/.orca-state/bin/lock-held-alert (scripts/lock-held-alert, installed in README step 1): it passes lockf's exit code through, counts the consecutive exit-75 rounds in <lock file>.skips.json next to the lock file (a gap of more than 15 minutes since the last skipped round starts a new count), alerts ops-system once (kind heartbeat_stale, source lock-held-alert) when 45 minutes have passed since the first skipped round, and reports recovery once the lock is taken again (sent again by a later round if it could not be sent); it prints no @@HB. The round that reports recovery posts once more after heartbeat-watch (curl at most 20 s): 296 + 4 + 20 = 320 s, under 330

before.name: ops · 29 心跳互查（盯 box ops · 29）

set.precheck: $HOME/.orca-state/bin/lock-held-alert /usr/bin/lockf -k -t 0 $HOME/.orca-state/heartbeat-watch/5c2d0575.lock $HOME/.orca-state/bin/heartbeat-watch.sh --precheck --target "box ops · 29 卡住检查心跳|grok-bot|94e4b0bc-0f9d-4cf2-a1fd-2282a888fe80|20" --target "MBA ops · 29 心跳互查|mba|<MBA 新任务 id>|20"

edit.why: one night with both watchers: keep the box target as it is (checked first, unchanged) and add the MBA task; two targets read through Orca environments (no ssh cap): worst 2 x 286 s = 572 s, plus about 4 s to start and at most 20 s for lock-held-alert's recovery post = 596 s, so 600 (Orca's maximum). 600 s is longer than the 5 min schedule, so the precheck runs under /usr/bin/lockf -k -t 0 with its own lock file, as the MBA task does (the directory already exists on the iMac), under lock-held-alert as well (install it on the iMac before this edit, README step 4); nobody watches 5c2d0575, so its lock-held alert (to ops-system) is the only report when its lock stays held

set.name: ops · 29 心跳互查（盯 MBA ops · 29）
set.precheck: $HOME/.orca-state/bin/lock-held-alert /usr/bin/lockf -k -t 0 $HOME/.orca-state/heartbeat-watch/5c2d0575.lock $HOME/.orca-state/bin/heartbeat-watch.sh --precheck --target "MBA ops · 29 心跳互查|mba|<MBA 新任务 id>|20"

edit.why: after the parallel night: drop the box target before box 94e4b0bc is disabled; keep lockf and lock-held-alert with the same lock file as the parallel stage (a round that outlives the 5 min schedule must not run next to the next one); one target, worst 286 s plus about 4 s to start = 290 s, so 300 stays, about 10 s to spare. A round that reports recovery after a lock-held alert posts once more (curl at most 20 s), about 310 s: Orca kills it and records a timeout; lock-held-alert writes the pending recovery to the state file before posting, so a later round sends it (README 已知限制). Nobody watches 5c2d0575: when its lock stays held, its own lock-held alert (to ops-system) is the only report. The rename is not in the brief, drop 'name' here if it is not wanted
